style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings. Ecclesiastes uses Elohim throughout — the divine name YHWH never appears in the book and is never inserted.
chapterNote: The book ends with its two most famous passages back to back. First, the allegory of aging (vv. 1-7), the most haunting poem on growing old ever written: the body as a great house going dark -- trembling keepers for the hands, bowed strong men for the legs, the few grinders, the dimming windows, the shut doors, the silenced daughters of music -- until the silver cord snaps, the golden bowl is crushed, the pitcher shatters at the spring, and the dust returns to the earth while the spirit returns to God who gave it. The charge that opens it is therefore urgent: remember your Creator now, in the days of your youth, before the evil days come. Verse 8 closes the frame -- vapor of vapors, the book's first words become its last -- and then the epilogue commends the Preacher's craft (goads and well-driven nails, given by one Shepherd) and hands down the conclusion of the whole matter: fear God and keep His commandments, for this is the whole of man, and God will bring every work into judgment, every hidden thing, whether good or evil.

1.text: Remember your Creator now, in the days of your youth, before the evil days come and the years arrive of which you will say, 'They hold no pleasure for me';
1.amp: Remember [zakar] now your Creator [bara -- the One who created you] in the days [yom] of your youth [bechuroth], while the evil [ra] days come [bo] not, nor the years [shanah] draw nigh [naga], when you shall say [amar], 'I have no pleasure [chephets] in them';
1.notes: zakar (H2142), the remembering charged in 11:8, now given its true object: the bara (H1254), the Creator -- the verb of Genesis 1:1. Remembering is covenant loyalty, not mere recall, and its season is bechuroth (H979), the prime years, before chephets (H2656), pleasure itself, wears out.

2.text: before the sun and the light, the moon and the stars grow dark, and the clouds come back again after the rain;
2.amp: While the sun [shemesh], or the light [or], or the moon [yareach], or the stars [kokab], be not darkened [chashak], nor the clouds [av] return [shub] after [achar] the rain [geshem]:
2.notes: In old age the sky itself seems to dim, and the clouds shub (H7725), return, after every rain: sorrows that once cleared now roll straight back in. The lights of creation's fourth day going out one by one open the poem of the body's un-creation.

3.text: in the day when the keepers of the house tremble and the strong men stoop, when the grinders cease because they are few, and those looking out through the windows are darkened,
3.amp: In the day [yom] when the keepers [shamar] of the house [bayith] shall tremble [zua], and the strong [chayil] men [enosh] shall bow [avat] themselves, and the grinders [tochanoth] cease [batel] because they are few [maat], and those that look out [raah] of the windows [arubbah] be darkened [chashak],
3.notes: The body as a bayith (H1004), a great house: the keepers (the hands) tremble, the chayil-men (the legs) bow, the grinders (the teeth, H2912) fall idle and few, and the windows (the eyes, arubbah, H699) go dim. batel (H988), to cease -- each servant of the house retiring in turn.

4.text: when the doors onto the street are shut and the sound of the mill runs low, when a man rises at the chirp of a bird, and all the daughters of song are bowed low;
4.amp: And the doors [delet] shall be shut [sagar] in the streets [shuq], when the sound [qol] of the grinding [tachanah] is low [shaphal]; and he shall rise up [qum] at the voice [qol] of the bird [tsippor], and all the daughters [bath] of musick [shir] shall be brought low [shachah];
4.notes: The shut doors are the ears (and the lips) closing to the street's noise; the mill-sound of eating and speech runs shaphal (H8217), low. Sleep grows so thin a tsippor's chirp ends it, yet the bath shir (H1323, H7892), the daughters of song -- voice and hearing both -- are bowed past enjoying any music.

5.text: when men are afraid of heights and terrors wait along the road, when the almond tree blossoms white, the grasshopper drags itself along, and the caperberry fails -- because man is going to his everlasting home, and the mourners are already circling in the street --
5.amp: Also when they shall be afraid [yare] of that which is high [gaboah], and fears shall be in the way [derek], and the almond tree [shaqed] shall blossom, and the grasshopper [chagab] shall be a burden [saval -- drag itself along as a load], and desire [abiyyonah -- the caperberry] shall fail [parar -- be annulled]: because man [adam] goes [halak] to his long [olam] home [bayith -- 'his everlasting home'], and the mourners [saphad] go about [savav] the streets [shuq]:
5.notes: The shaqed (H8247), the almond, flowers white before its leaves: the crown of white hair. The chagab (H2284), the grasshopper -- lightness itself -- now a saval (H5445), a burden dragged; and the abiyyonah (H35), the caperberry that stirred appetite, parar (H6565), fails. The destination is the bayith olam, the everlasting home, and the saphad (H5594), the professional mourners, already pace the street.

6.text: before the silver cord snaps and the golden bowl is crushed, before the pitcher is shattered at the spring and the wheel broken at the cistern,
6.amp: Or ever the silver [keseph] cord [chebel] be loosed [rachaq -- removed, snapped], or the golden [zahab] bowl [gullah] be broken [ratsats -- crushed], or the pitcher [kad] be broken [shabar -- shattered] at the fountain [mabbua -- the spring], or the wheel [galgal] broken [ratsats] at the cistern [bor].
6.notes: Two pictures of the same instant: the golden lamp-bowl swinging on its silver chebel (H2256) until the cord gives and the light spills out, and the well whose kad and galgal -- pitcher and wheel -- shatter so the water can no longer be drawn. ratsats (H7533), crushed: light and water, the two oldest figures for life, both cut off at once.

7.text: and the dust goes back to the earth it came from, and the spirit returns home to God who gave it.
7.amp: Then shall the dust [afar] return [shub] to the earth [eretz] as it was: and the spirit [ruach] shall return [shub] unto God [Elohim] who gave [natan] it.
7.notes: The double shub (H7725): afar (H6083) down to the eretz of Genesis 3:19, and the ruach (H7307) up to Elohim -- the question of 3:21 answered at last. Since the breath was natan (H5414), given, it goes home to the Giver; man's two ingredients each return to their source.

8.text: Vapor of vapors, says the Preacher; all of it is vapor.
8.amp: Vapor of vapors [hebel], says [amar] the preacher [Qoheleth]; all is vapor [hebel].
8.notes: The book closes its frame with its opening words (cf. 1:2): hebel (H1892), the breath-verdict, now spoken over a finished argument rather than ahead of one. Everything under the sun remains vapor -- which is exactly why the epilogue's conclusion looks above it.

9.text: Besides being wise himself, the Preacher also went on teaching the people knowledge; he weighed and searched out and set in order many proverbs.
9.amp: And moreover [yother], because the preacher [Qoheleth] was wise [chakam], he still taught [lamad] the people [am] knowledge [daat]; yea, he gave good heed [azan -- listened carefully, weighed], and sought out [chaqar -- searched, examined], and set in order [taqan] many [rabah] proverbs [mashal].
9.notes: The epilogue commends the craft: azan (H239), to weigh with the ear; chaqar (H2713), to search to the bottom; taqan (H8626), the straightening-verb of 1:15 and 7:13 -- what no man can do to the world's crookedness, the teacher at least did to his proverbs (mashal, H4912). Wisdom kept teaching (lamad, H3925) the am, the ordinary people.

10.text: The Preacher sought to find words of delight, and what he wrote was upright -- words of truth.
10.amp: The preacher [Qoheleth] sought [baqash] to find out [matsa] acceptable words ['words of delight', chephets dabar, the KJV margin]: and that which was written [kathab] was upright [yosher], even words [dabar] of truth [emeth].
10.notes: Three standards in one sentence: delight (chephets, H2656 -- words worth reading), yosher (H3476, straightness), and emeth (H571, truth). matsa (H4672), the finding-verb the book kept denying, succeeds here -- the right words can be found, and Scripture is where he put them.

11.text: The words of the wise are like goads, and the collected sayings like nails driven firm -- given by one Shepherd.
11.amp: The words [dabar] of the wise [chakam] are as goads [dorban -- the ox-goad], and as nails [masmer] fastened [nata -- planted, driven firm] by the masters [baal] of assemblies [asuppah -- the collections], which are given [natan] from one [echad] shepherd [roeh].
11.notes: Two functions of true words: the dorban (H1861) that jabs the ox forward, and the masmer driven nata (H5193), planted deep, to hang a life on. The asuppah (H627) are the gathered collections -- and behind every wise collector stands the echad roeh (H259, H7462), the one Shepherd whose giving (natan, H5414) makes the words Scripture (cf. Psalm 23:1).

12.text: And beyond these, my son, be warned: of the making of many books there is no end, and much study wears out the flesh.
12.amp: And further [yother], by these, my son [ben], be admonished [zahar -- warned]: of making [asah] many [rabah] books [sepher] there is no end [qets]; and much [rabah] study ['reading', the KJV margin] is a weariness [yegiah] of the flesh [basar].
12.notes: The teacher's aside to his ben (H1121): the library is infinite and you are not. zahar (H2094), the warning-word of 4:13 -- beyond the words the one Shepherd gives, book-making runs on without qets (H7093), and yegiah (H3024), weariness, is all the flesh gets from chasing it.

13.text: The end of the matter, all having been heard: fear God and keep His commandments, for this is the whole of man.
13.amp: Let us hear [shama] the conclusion [soph -- the end] of the whole matter [dabar]: Fear [yare] God [Elohim], and keep [shamar] His commandments [mitsvah]: for this is the whole ['the whole duty', the KJV supplies 'duty'] of man [adam].
13.notes: The Hebrew reads simply 'this is the whole of adam' -- not one duty among many but the entire shape of a human life. yare (H3372) and shamar (H8104), fearing and keeping: reverence rooted inward, obedience worked outward. After every experiment, the soph (H5490) is two verbs long.

14.text: For God will bring every work into judgment, along with every hidden thing, whether it is good or whether it is evil.
14.amp: For God [Elohim] shall bring [bo] every work [maaseh] into judgment [mishpat], with every secret thing [alam -- every hidden thing], whether it be good [tov], or whether it be evil [ra].
14.notes: The final answer to the crooked courtroom of 3:16 and the slow sentences of 8:11: mishpat (H4941) is coming for kol maaseh, every work, and alam (H5956), the hidden things, are on the docket too. Under the sun the books never balanced; before this bench they all will (cf. 2 Corinthians 5:10).
